newsitem.title: USA: Ukraine officials try to shore up business climate.
newsitem.headline: Ukraine officials try to shore up business climate.

text.p: Ukrainian officials on Thursday sought to assure Washington their government is addressing problems ranging from economic reforms to the dumping of steel on the U.S. market.

Discussions within a new Ukrainian-American cooperation commission "will help us to renew trust between our two nations and boost development," Roman Shpek, head of Ukraine's National Agency for Reconstruction and Development, told a news conference.

Ukrainian President Leonid Kuchma, in Washington to meet with U.S. and international banking officials, wants to make it clear his country "is faithful to the course of economic reforms" and restore trust in that process, Shpek added.
He said initial talks have taken place in an atmosphere where the parties were "friends and partners."

Ukraine is due to receive $330 million in U.S. grants and $650 million in loans this year. But the country has been criticised in the West for alleged widespread corruption, an unstable investment climate and mountains of red tape.

Last month the Group of Seven industrialised countries said it was "increasingly concerned that the Ukrainian government has been unable to implement the ambitious reform agenda developed in cooperation with the International Monetary Fund."

Shpek said Kuchma was meeting with members of Congress on Thursday and that Representative Sonny Callahan, an Alabama Republican and a critic of Ukrainian steel sales in the United States, has said he would oppose further assistance unless the steel issue is resolved.
He said the matter was being discussed within the new cooperation committee -- which is chaired by Vice President Al Gore and Kuchma -- and "we believe we will be able to come to a solution."

He also said a number of companies, including Boeing, Cargill, General Electric, Siemens and Royal Dutch Shell, have agreed to serve on an advisory committee that will consult with Kuchma on the problems faced by foreign firms trying to do business in Ukraine.
Ukrainian Finance Minister Ihor Mityukov told the same news conference that the country's parliament is attempting to simplify access to Ukrainian markets for both domestic and outside investors.
